For **one standard electric blanket for an 8-hour night**, I’d look at the **BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh)**. One comparison names it as its top pick and estimates about **12 hours for a 150 W blanket** because blankets cycle on and off; another guide estimates a 1,024 Wh station will run a blanket averaging 100 W for roughly **8 hours**. ([Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket), [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/))

Check the wattage on your blanket’s label: runtime varies a lot with the blanket’s setting and how often it cycles. If you want a safer margin—especially for a high-draw blanket or two blankets—consider a larger station. One estimate puts a queen blanket averaging 260 W at about **2,600 Wh for 8 hours**. ([HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/))

Plug the blanket directly into the station, and keep the station off the bed and away from the blanket. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night))
